newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean ends mixed in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean ends mixed in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in slow trading on Monday, with most investors on the sidelines, traders said.
The key January 1997 contract ended at an intra-day high of 3,192 yuan ($384) per tonne, losing four yuan. It opened at a low of 3,190.
March fell seven to 3,230 and May 10 to 3,320, July rose 20 to 3,360 and September 10 to 3,370 and November was unchanged at 3,400. Combined volume fell to 14,000 tonnes from 15,950.
Traders said many investors continued to take a wait-and-see attitude due to a lack of market-moving news.
"Despite poor fundamentals, it is hard for soybean to fall sharply due to the absence of heavy selling," one trader said.
"The more active stock market today also attracted many investors," he added.
Traders expect soybean to move around 3,200 yuan in the next few days.
